'''Quentin Lamar Richardson''' (born April 13, 1980) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who was formerly the director of player development for the [[Detroit Pistons]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Nicknamed "'''Q-Ball'''", he played professionally for 13 seasons for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], [[Phoenix Suns]], [[New York Knicks]], [[Miami Heat]], and [[Orlando Magic]]. He won the [[NBA Three-Point Contest]] in 2005.

==Early years==
Richardson was born in [[Chicago]], [[Illinois]] to Lee and Emma Richardson where he attended [[Whitney M. Young Magnet High School|Whitney Young High School]]. In 1998, he led the Dolphins to the state AA title.  In 2006, Richardson was voted as one of the [[100 Legends of the IHSA Boys Basketball Tournament]], a group of former players and coaches in honor of the 100 year anniversary of the [[Illinois High School Boys Basketball Championship|IHSA boys basketball tournament]].

==Collegiate career==
Richardson played college basketball for [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul University]] where he averaged 17.9 points and 10.2 rebounds per game in two seasons. He became the only player in school history to have 1,000+ points, 500+ rebounds and 100+ [[three-point field goal]]s. As a freshman, he earned both the Conference USA Player of the Year and Freshman of the Year. Richardson declared for the [[NBA draft]] after his sophomore year in 2000.

==Professional career==
===Los Angeles Clippers (2000–2004)===
Richardson was drafted by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] with the 18th pick of the [[2000 NBA draft]]. He was selected after fellow Clippers [[Darius Miles]] and [[Keyon Dooling]]. Richardson  would star in a documentary with Miles entitled ''The Youngest Guns'' which chronicled their first three seasons in the NBA with the Clippers. 

Richardson's debut game was played on October 31, 2000 in a 94 - 107 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]] where he recorded 2 points and 2 rebounds in 7 minutes of playing time.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/200010310UTA.html | title=Clippers vs Jazz, October 31, 2000 }}</ref> In his first game as a starter on November 29, 2000, Richardson played 43 minutes and recorded 18 points, 8 rebounds, 1 assist and 1 steal in a 103 - 86 victory over the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/200011290LAC.html | title=Warriors vs Clippers, November 29, 2000 }}</ref>

On New Year's Eve 2003, Richardson posted a career-high 44 points in a 120 - 104 victory over the [[Denver Nuggets]]. It was the only time in Richardson's 13-year career where he scored 40 points or more. 

Richardson spent four seasons with the Clippers playing in 281 games (starting 105 of them) and averaging 12.0 points, 4.6 rebounds and 1.4 assists at 25.7 minutes per game.

===Phoenix Suns (2004–2005)===
Richardson signed a six-year, $45 million contract with the [[Phoenix Suns]] as a free agent on July 29, 2004.<ref name="suns">{{cite web| url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/zquentin_richardson_040729.html | title=Suns Sign Quentin Richardson | work=[[NBA.com]] | date=July 29, 2004 | access-date=August 14, 2009}}</ref>

The [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05 season]] was a big one for not only Richardson, but the Suns as well. He set a new Suns single-season record for [[three-point field goal]]s, eclipsing the previous record of 199 set by [[Dan Majerle]]. He finished the season with a league-leading 631 three-point attempts, and 226 three-point field goals,<ref name="sunsknicks">{{cite web| url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2096710 | title=Suns send first-round pick Robinson to Knicks | work=[[ESPN]] | date=June 29, 2005 | access-date=August 14, 2009}}</ref> co-leading the league with [[Kyle Korver]]. Richardson's single-season three-point record was surpassed by [[Collin Gillespie]] in the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Collin Gillespie breaks Suns' franchise record for most 3-pointers in a season|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/collin-gillespie-breaks-suns-franchise-record-for-most-3-pointers-in-a-season|access-date=June 21, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}}</ref> Richardson also set a Suns franchise record with nine threes against the [[2004–05 New Orleans Hornets season|New Orleans Hornets]] on December 29, 2004.<ref name="sunsknicks" /> Richardson would also go on to win the NBA All-Star Three-Point Shootout that same season.<ref name="spokesman">{{cite news |last= |first= |date=February 20, 2005|title=Smith pays homage to Wilkins in victory |url= https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2005/feb/20/smith-pays-homage-to-wilkins-in-victory/|work= [[The Spokesman-Review]]|location= [[Denver]]|access-date=March 20, 2024}}</ref> The Suns finished the regular season with a league-best 62 wins and 20 losses. He made his playoff debut with the Suns [[2005 NBA Playoffs|in 2005]] who would eventually lose to the eventual champion [[San Antonio Spurs]] in the [[Western Conference (NBA)|Western Conference]] Finals.

On November 20, 2024 on his Knuckleheads Podcast with [[Darius Miles]], Richardson revealed that his sole season in Phoenix was his favorite season of his entire NBA career. Citing that he had the most fun playing with his teammates, the rising stardom of his fellow teammates such as [[Steve Nash]] and [[Amar'e Stoudemire]] and how the Suns were able to shock the league by making a deep playoff run to the Western Conference Finals.

===New York Knicks (2005–2009)===
Richardson was traded from the Suns, along with [[2005 NBA Draft|2005 draft]] pick [[Nate Robinson]], to the New York Knicks in exchange for [[Kurt Thomas (basketball)|Kurt Thomas]] and [[Dijon Thompson]] on June 28, 2005.<ref name="sunsknicks" />
His first three seasons in New York were largely hampered by nagging injuries—the most serious being a chronic back condition—which limited him to 55, 49, and 65 games played respectively. His injury situation finally stabilized during the 2008–2009 season, when he remained healthy enough to appear in all but seven games. This does not include two additional DNP-CDs (Did Not Play – Coach's Decision) that he received; one on February 28, 2009, against the [[2008–09 Miami Heat season|Miami Heat]] and a second on March 10, 2009, against the [[2008–09 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]].

=== Miami Heat (2009–2010) ===
During the 2009 offseason, Richardson was traded four times within a 49-day timespan. On the [[2009 NBA Draft|2009 draft day]] (June 25, 2009), Richardson was first traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in exchange for [[Darko Miličić]].<ref name="knicksgrizzlies">{{cite web| url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies_acquire_quentin_richardson-090625.html | title=Grizzlies acquire swingman Quentin Richardson from Knicks | work=[[NBA.com]] | date=June 29, 2009 | access-date=August 14, 2009}}</ref> His stint with the Grizzlies was very short as he was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in exchange for [[Zach Randolph]] just 22 days later on July 17, 2009.<ref name="grizzliesclippers">{{cite web| url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/breakingnews090717.html | title=Clippers Acquire Quentin Richardson From Memphis in Exchange for Zach Randolph | work=[[NBA.com]] | date=July 17, 2009 | access-date=August 14, 2009}}</ref> His second stint with the Clippers only lasted for three days as on July 20, 2009, he was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for [[Sebastian Telfair]], [[Mark Madsen (basketball)|Mark Madsen]], and [[Craig Smith (basketball, born 1983)|Craig Smith]].<ref name="clipperswolves">{{cite web| url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/Timberwolves_acquire_Quentin_Richardson-090720.html | title=Timberwolves acquire Quentin Richardson from Clippers | work=[[NBA.com]] | date=July 20, 2009 | access-date=August 14, 2009}}</ref>

Finally, after being a member of the Timberwolves for just 24 days, Richardson was traded for the fourth time on August 13, 2009, this time to the [[Miami Heat]] for [[Mark Blount]].<ref name="wolvesheat">{{cite web| url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat_acquire_quentin_richardso_2009_08_14.html | title=HEAT Acquire Quentin Richardson from Minnesota | work=[[NBA.com]] | date=August 14, 2009 | access-date=August 14, 2009}}</ref> Richardson would be a consistent starting Small Forward for the Heat, starting in 75 of the 76 games he played while averaging 8.9 points and 4.9 rebounds.

===Orlando Magic (2010–2012)===
In 2010, Richardson signed a three-year, $7.5 million contract with the [[Orlando Magic]]. He remained with the team until October 2012, when he was waived. During his 2-year stint with Orlando, Richardson played 105 games and averaged 4.4 points, 0.7 assists and 2.9 rebounds while shooting 31.5% from the 3pt-line.

===Return to New York (2013)===
On April 16, 2013, Richardson signed with the [[New York Knicks]] for the remainder of the season,<ref name=raskin>{{cite web|last=Raskin|first=Alex|title=Quentin Richardson rejoins Knicks|url=http://www.nj.com/knicks/index.ssf/2013/04/quentin_richardson_rejoins_kni.html|work=NJ.com|date=April 16, 2013|access-date=April 16, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://knicksnow.com/posts/3224/knicks-ink-quentin-richardson#.UW-VSUopm_I | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130418233620/http://knicksnow.com/posts/3224/knicks-ink-quentin-richardson#.UW-VSUopm_I | url-status=dead | archive-date=April 18, 2013 | title=Knicks Ink Quentin Richardson | work=Knicksnow.com | date=April 16, 2013 | access-date=April 18, 2013 }}</ref> joining that team for a second time. He only played one regular season game, scoring five points in twenty nine minutes on 1 for 11 shooting, but brought down ten rebounds.  He did appear in five playoff games, hitting two three-pointers in New York's 26-point blowout win of the Pacers in Game 2 of the Eastern Conference semifinals.

On July 10, 2013, Richardson was part of a trade package to the [[Toronto Raptors]], along with center [[Marcus Camby]], forward [[Steve Novak]], a first-round draft pick in 2016, and two second-round draft picks in 2014 and 2017, in exchange for forward [[Andrea Bargnani]].<ref name=raptors>{{cite web|url=http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/nyktrade_071013/ |title=Raptors Acquire Three Players, Three Picks From Knicks |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=July 10, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006152814/http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/nyktrade_071013/ |archive-date=October 6, 2014 }}</ref>

Richardson's final NBA game was played on May 11, 2013, in Game 3 of the Eastern Conference Semi-Finals against the [[2012–13 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana Pacers]]. Richardson played less than two minutes and the only stat he recorded was one rebound. On September 3, Richardson was waived by the Raptors.<ref name=raptors1>{{cite web | url=http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/richardson-090313/ | title=Raptors Waive Quentin Richardson | work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. | date=September 3, 2013 | access-date=September 3, 2013 | archive-date=January 6, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150106024042/http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/richardson-090313/ | url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Post-playing career==
On August 7, 2014, it was announced that Richardson was named the director of player development for the [[Detroit Pistons]].

{{Asof|2014}} he worked for the Bally Sports Orlando Magic broadcast team.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-add-coaching-and-basketball-operations-staffs | title = Detroit Pistons Add to Coaching and Basketball Operations Staffs | publisher = [[Detroit Pistons]] | date = August 7, 2014 | access-date = August 7, 2014 }}</ref>

He currently co-hosts the ''Knuckleheads'' podcast with [[Darius Miles]] for ''[[The Players' Tribune]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theplayerstribune.com/collections/knuckleheadspod|title=Knuckleheads with Quentin Richardson and Darius Miles |work=ThePlayersTribune.com |accessdate=May 1, 2022}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In 1992, Richardson lost his mother to [[breast cancer]], his grandmother to natural causes, and also his brother, Bernard, who was shot and killed in Chicago, aged 23.<ref name="bernard">[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2250907 Richardson's brother shot, killed in Chicago]. ESPN.</ref> Another of Richardson's brothers, Lee Jr., was murdered on December 5, 2005, in Chicago during a robbery.<ref name="bernard" /><ref name="leejr">[https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/brother-of-knicks-richardson-murdered-1.550167 Brother of Knicks' Richardson murdered]. [[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]].</ref> Richardson has another older brother, Cedric, and one older sister Rochelle. Richardson is also the cousin of multi entrepreneur Dean Richardson.

Richardson was engaged for 14 months to R&B singer [[Brandy Norwood|Brandy]]. They split in September 2005.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realitytvworld.com/news/brandy-breaks-off-engagement-quentin-richardson-morphs-tattoo-1005596.php|title=Brandy breaks off engagement to Quentin Richardson, morphs tattoo|date=October 28, 2005|access-date=August 6, 2020}}</ref>

Richardson has appeared in multiple acting roles, most notably as himself in the 2002 film ''[[Van Wilder]]''.
